newsitem.title: USA: US Air's expanded suit seen having minimal effect.
newsitem.headline: US Air's expanded suit seen having minimal effect.

text.p: US Airways Group Inc intensified its attack against British Airways Plc, but industry experts doubted the new ammunition will yield greater results.
US Airways said Wednesday it expanded its existing lawsuit against British Airways, to include alleged breach of fiduciary duty by BA's representatives on the US Airways board.
"There's not an awful lot of substance to it. The have a hard row to hoe to prove fidiciary negligence," said Timothy Ross, an analyst with SBC Warburg.
British Airways said the amended lawsuit shows US Airways' original lawsuit was "completely without merit and likely to have been dismissed by the court."

Other analysts suggested that USAirways' would have to step carefully with its new allegations against the former board members. If USAirways successfully proves BA members were negligent, shareholders then could argue that USAirways itself was negligent for not properly overseeing the activities of its board, analysts said.
Three British Airways representatives resigned from US Airway's board in January as the two carriers continued to dismantle a turbulent relationship that began in 1993.
US Airways said Wednesday it also amended its initial antitrust and contract allegations in the suit filed with a federal court in New York last July.
US Airways, then called USAir, alleged that British Airways' proposed alliance with American Airlines violated the existing pact between USAirways and BA.
